**Panama City Beach, Florida**

Panama City Beach is the only Florida beach that lets visitors bring open‑container alcoholic beverages all year **except for the month of March**.  
The beach’s official website lists a one‑month alcohol‑ban (March) and says that 11 of the 12 months of the year allow drinking—provided the drinks are in plastic or other non‑glass containers.

> *“Eleven months out of the year, excluding March, alcohol consumption is allowed on Panama City Beach … Glass containers are prohibited year‑round.”*  
> – Visit Panama City Beach FAQ

So if you’re planning a beach trip and want to bring a drink with you (no glass), Panama City Beach is the place to go—just stay away from the sand in March.

*   [Author email](mailto:poet.wolfe@theadvocate.com "Email")

With the warm weather of spring emerging, people will start flocking to Gulf Coast beaches with the essentials: sunscreen, bathing suits and towels. Many will also have alcoholic beverages, from fizzy hard seltzers to ice-cold beer, clinking in beach bags.

But rules vary for the consumption of alcohol at the white sand beaches across the Gulf Coast, including those in Mississippi, Alabama and the Florida panhandle. Some allow vacationers and springbreakers who are 21 years or older to drink, though forbid glass containers, while others fully prohibit alcoholic beverages.

Perhaps you, like many other Louisianans — college students anticipating spring break and employees in need of a vacation — are preparing for a beach getaway.

![Image 18: overlay-clever](https://assets.cleverwebserver.com/Pixel.gif)![Image 19: close](https://assets.cleverwebserver.com/Close.png)[![Image 20: Logo](https://assets.cleverwebserver.com/CleverLogo.ico)](https://cleveradvertising.com/)

Here's a list of popular beaches in Mississippi, Alabama and the Florida panhandle that allow and do not allow alcoholic beverages.

### Mississippi

According to [government officials](https://harrisoncountyms.gov/how_do_i_/find_learn_about/sand_beach/rules_of_the_beach.php), glass containers are not allowed on the beaches of**Harrison County**, where Biloxi, Gulfport, Long Beach and Pass Christian are located. Its official website does not say that alcoholic beverages are prohibited.

Beaches in **Hancock County**, including those in Waveland and Bay St. Louis, allow vacationers to bring alcoholic beverages, though glass containers are not allowed, its Chamber of Commerce says.

![Image 21: beaches.0006.jpg](blob:http://localhost/17c37ca6bd634b99f272bb6ea5c29dd7)

Beachgoers hang out on the shores of the Bay St. Louis beach.

[By JULIA GUILBEAU | Staff writer](https://www.nola.com/users/profile/Julia%20Guilbeau)

For beaches in **Jackson County**, home to Ocean Springs and Pascagoula, its rules on alcohol vary. Mississippi's [tourism website](https://visitmississippi.org/things-to-do/beaches/ocean-springs-beaches/) does not explicitly say that people can't bring alcohol to Front and East Beaches in Ocean Springs, but it does warn of glass containers being prohibited.

As for Pascagoula, its parks and recreation department [states](https://cityofpascagoula.com/DocumentCenter/View/2884/General-Policies-for-City-Parks--Facilities) that no alcohol can be sold or consumed on city property without a permit.

### Alabama

A resort city in Baldwin County known for its blue-green water and fine white sand, **Gulf Shores** does not allow the consumption of alcohol on any of its beaches, according to [its website](https://www.gulfshoresal.gov/1138/Beach-Rules-Regulations).

![Image 22: beaches.0006.jpg](blob:http://localhost/17c37ca6bd634b99f272bb6ea5c29dd7)

People line the beach in Gulf Shores, Ala., on Friday, June 7, 2024. (Staff photo by Brett Duke, The Times-Picayune)

STAFF PHOTO BY BRETT DUKE

In**Orange Beach**, next door to Gulf Shores, alcohol is permitted, though [government officials warn](https://www.orangebeachal.gov/faq.aspx?qid=139)glass containers are prohibited.

Located on the tip of Dauphin Island, **West End Beach**allows vacationers to bring their own beverages, [its website](https://www.townofdauphinisland.org/faq)says, but similar to Orange Beach, glass containers are banned.

### Florida panhandle

**Destin**, a busy beach town known for its recreation and fishing opportunities, allows the consumption of alcohol, but prohibits glass containers, according to a representative on [its tourism website](https://www.destinfwb.com/explore/beaches/beach-flags-and-safety/).

Eleven months out of the year, excluding March, alcohol consumption is allowed on **Panama City Beach**, [its website](https://www.visitpanamacitybeach.com/plan-your-trip/faqs/) says. Glass containers are prohibited year-round.

The [tourism website](https://www.visitpensacola.com/blog/beach-safety/) for **Pensacola Beach**states that while glass containers and public displays of drunkenness are not allowed, alcoholic beverages are OK.

![Image 23: beaches.0006.jpg](blob:http://localhost/17c37ca6bd634b99f272bb6ea5c29dd7)

Beach goers brave the cold wind and water on Pensacola Beach, Fl. Saturday, April 3, 2021.

**Fort Walton**, a beach city within Oskaloosa County, prohibits alcohol consumption outside of state parks, according to a [vacation rentals website](https://www.ecvr.com/okaloosa-county-beach-regulations/).

Rosemary, Grayton and Seaside beaches, all of which are a part of the scenic 30A highway corridor, permits alcoholic beverages and open containers, another [vacation rentals website](https://www.rivardnet.com/blog/30a-beach-rules) says. Glass containers are not allowed.
